_comment: Processing-time multiplier sweep at the locked slack lambda (0.008, agv07_single) -- tests whether growing mean proc time toward the ~312s estimated per-machine interarrival gap (vs current mean ~52.5s from minProcTime=15/maxProcTime=90) shifts machine utilization up and dispatch decisions off their 92-99% degenerate rate (see decision_log.csv from results/0902e). mu/sigma are derived uniformly from minProcTime/maxProcTime by ConfigLoader ((min+max)/2, (max-min)/6) -- 1x reproduces the exact baseline already in results/0902e (included here for a self-contained comparison set; skip re-running it if reusing that data). 2x/4x/6x scale both bounds together, keeping the same proc-time distribution SHAPE (sigma/mu ratio constant) while moving the mean. Same instance/lambda/duration as the lambda dial-in (results/0902c) -- 15000s, dynamicJobCap=0 required. REQUIRES --baselinedrain true. Look at decision_log.csv is_degenerate rate by decision_type, plus machine_utilization.csv utilization_rate (watch it doesn't overshoot into a NEW saturation regime) and agv_performance.csv busy fraction (should stay roughly flat -- trip counts/transit times don't change with proc time).
